component_findings.actionability: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Messages normally provide enough precise information to correct the issue without requiring unrelated guesswork; suggested fixes count only when semantically reliable. Evidence basis: Compiled adversarial Go programs (syntax-invalid ADV-22a truncated file, ADV-22b garbled identifier) using go build from readable adversarial corpus, and inspected overflow-behavior programs (ADV-01) for observable diagnostics. | go build on truncated ADV-22a produced: 'adv22a/main.go:9:1: syntax error: unexpected EOF, expected }' -- includes file, exact line:column, and expected-token hint. | Compiler errors are terse but precise (single line, file:line:col, short message); no multi-line caret-highlighted source snippets like Rust/clang, no suggested fixes emitted by the compiler itself (editor tooling like gopls provides more, which is Ecosystem not Language Quality). | Go's error model surfaces domain errors as explicit values (multi-return, error interface) inspectable by static tools but without compiler-level provenance like Rust's Result diagnostics. | Runtime: nil-pointer dereference and index-out-of-range panics include a stack trace with file:line, but signed integer truncation (ADV-01 int32(int64(...))) truncates silently with no diagnostic -- a real diagnostics gap versus checked-arithmetic languages. | go vet and the race detector (-race) provide additional static/runtime diagnostics but are opt-in tools, not innate compiler diagnostics for ordinary builds.

component_findings.abstraction_reuse: Recertified level 3 under the current criterion: Functions, modules/types and generic/polymorphic abstraction support reusable composition across ordinary programs. Evidence basis: Inspected micro/ and adversarial/ Go program corpus for expressiveness signals: generics (Go 1.18+), goroutines/channels, defer/panic/recover, slices/maps as built-ins, multiple return values, implicit-interface polymorphism, error-as-value idiom. | Go lacks algebraic data types / tagged unions, exhaustive pattern matching, and operator overloading, reducing expressiveness relative to Rust/Kotlin/Swift. | No macro/metaprogramming system; reflection is limited and verbose (reflect package). | Generics exist since 1.18 but with restricted type-set constraints and no specialization, limiting generic-code expressiveness compared to Rust traits or C++ templates. | Error handling via explicit multi-value returns is explicit and simple but verbose (repeated if err != nil boilerplate); no try/? operator equivalent. | Concurrency primitives (goroutines, channels, select) are a strong expressiveness feature, enabling concise CSP-style concurrent code not directly available in many peer languages without libraries. | No built-in sum types/enums beyond simple iota constants; no null-safety type system (nil pointers/interfaces still possible). | Standard library favors composition (interfaces, embedding) over inheritance -- adequate but sometimes limits expressing polymorphic hierarchies concisely.
